name: Peregrine Falcon
note: Fastest animal on Earth — dive speeds over 320 km/h.

name: Great Horned Owl
note: Tufted 'horns' are feathers, not ears — its real ears sit asymmetrically for pinpoint hearing.

name: Northern Cardinal
note: Males sing year-round; pairs often feed together, beaks touching.

name: Blue Jay
note: An intelligent corvid that mimics hawks and caches thousands of acorns each fall.

name: Atlantic Puffin
note: Holds up to 60 fish at once thanks to backward-pointing spines in its beak.

name: Bald Eagle
note: Eyesight roughly 4-5x sharper than a human's.

name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
note: Wings beat up to 80 times per second; crosses the Gulf of Mexico nonstop.

name: Greater Flamingo
note: Pink comes from carotenoid pigments in its food — born grey, turns pink.

name: Emperor Penguin
note: Huddles through -60°C winters; males fast up to 4 months incubating the egg.

name: Common Kingfisher
note: Dives up to 1m deep with sealed eyelids and a perfectly aimed plunge.

name: Snowy Owl
note: Nomadic hunter; irrupts south in big numbers when lemmings crash.

name: Scarlet Macaw
note: Lives 40-50 years in the wild and pairs for life.
